question: In Arc 6, I was surprised at the time by the decision to leave Julius with a permanent scar on his face—you took quite a bold step with a character who is so good-looking. Was this something you had planned in advance as part of the story? Nowadays, we often see him touching the scar, but will he never go back to the gesture of playing with his bangs?
answer:
I've talked about this from time to time, but I'm the type of person who doesn't really picture things in my head when I'm writing. There are two types of novelists: people who picture an image in their heads and then turn it into prose, and people who have things come to them as prose in the first place. I'm the latter type. So, to make sure I don't forget the visual details, I give my characters distinctive features and habits.

Things like Emilia's silver hair and Reinhard's red hair. By giving them those kinds of distinctive characteristics and keeping them in mind, I make sure I don't forget what they look like. Julius frequently touching the scar under his eye is a habit I gave him so that I don't forget it.

As for the question of why I put a scar on Julius's face in the first place, I didn't do it—Reid did it, so... (laughs).

Of course, I put together the plot (the rough framework of the story) before I start writing, but I hadn't decided on something as specific as “Julius will have a scar left on him when his battle with Reid ends.” While I was writing, I think I came up with the idea that it would be good to portray Reid leaving a scar, with Julius feeling a little proud that he now has a scar from having fought the First Sword Saint.

In particular, with good scenes, what happens is the result of each character's emotional outbursts and their actions in each individual moment, so I'd like you to think of it as something that “happened as a result of the characters colliding with one another.”

The gesture of playing with his bangs will probably come back, too. For some reason, I have this image of him touching the scar with his left hand and playing with his hair with his right.
